ai.description: The Indian Cobra reaches 1–1.5 meters. It is typically brown, yellow, or black with a distinctive hood marked by a spectacle-shaped pattern on the rear. It possesses a broad, flattened neck.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Naja naja* is the distinctive "spectacle" pattern on the rear of its hood, which lacks the closed-loop ocelli found in other cobras.
ai.habitat: The Indian cobra inhabits diverse environments, including grasslands, scrublands, and agricultural fields, ranging from sea level up to 2,000 meters in altitude.
ai.behavior: When threatened, the Indian cobra adopts a defensive posture by raising its forebody and expanding its neck ribs to form a distinctive hood to appear larger to predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Indian cobra is oviparous, laying clutches of 10–30 eggs between April and July. Hatching typically occurs after an incubation period of roughly 48 to 69 days.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Indian Cobra is widespread across the Indian subcontinent, inhabiting diverse landscapes from sea level up to 2,000 meters in elevation throughout most of India.
